questions.q: The domain of the function $\sqrt{\dfrac{x-7}{9-x}}$ is
questions.explanation: We need $\dfrac{x-7}{9-x}\ge0$ with $x\neq9$. This holds for $7\le x<9$, i.e. the domain is $[7,9)$.

questions.q: If $n(A)=2$ and the number of relations from set A to set B is 1024, then $n(B)$ is
questions.explanation: Number of relations $=2^{n(A)\cdot n(B)}=2^{2n(B)}=1024=2^{10}\Rightarrow 2n(B)=10\Rightarrow n(B)=5$.

questions.q: Let R be the relation in the set N given by $R=\{(a,b):a=b-2,b>6\}$. Which of the following is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: Checking $(6,8)$: $a=6=b-2=8-2$ and $b=8>6$, so it satisfies both conditions.

questions.q: $f(x)=(x+1)^2$ for $x\ge1$. $g(x)$ is a function whose graph is the reflection of the graph of $f(x)$ in the line $y=x$, then $g(x)$ is
questions.explanation: $g$ is the inverse of $f$. From $y=(x+1)^2$ with $x\ge1$, $x+1=\sqrt y$ (positive root), so $x=\sqrt y-1$, i.e. $g(x)=\sqrt x-1$.

questions.q: Domain of the function f, given by $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x-2)(x-5)}}$ is
questions.explanation: Need (x-2)(x-5) > 0 (strictly, since it is under a square root in a denominator), giving x < 2 or x > 5.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \sin([\pi^2]x) - \sin([-\pi^2]x)$, where $[x]$ = greatest integer $\leq x$, then which of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: $[\pi^2]=9,[-\pi^2]=-10$, so $f(x)=\sin 9x+\sin 10x$; $f(\pi)=\sin9\pi+\sin10\pi=0$, not $-1$, so option (4) is false.

questions.q: Let A = {a, b, c}, then the number of equivalence relations on A containing (b, c) is
questions.explanation: Either {a},{b,c} as separate classes, or the full set {a,b,c} as one class — both are equivalence relations containing (b,c), giving 2.

questions.q: Let the functions "f" and "g" be $f: [0, \pi/2] \to R$ given by $f(x)=\sin x$ and $g:[0,\pi/2]\to R$ given by $g(x)=\cos x$, where R is the set of real numbers. Consider the following statements: Statement (I): f and g are one-one. Statement (II): f + g is one-one. Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement (I) is true, statement (II) is false
Statement (I) is false, statement (II) is true
questions.explanation: sinx and cosx are each monotonic on $[0,\pi/2]$ hence one-one, but $f+g=\sqrt2\sin(x+\pi/4)$ rises then falls on this interval, so it is not one-one.

Let $f:R\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$. Then the pre images of 17 and -3 respectively are
questions.explanation: $x^2+1=17\Rightarrow x=\pm4$. $x^2+1=-3$ has no real solution since $x^2+1\ge1$, so its preimage is $\phi$.

questions.q: Let $(gof)(x)=\sin x$ and $(fog)(x)=(\sin\sqrt x)^2$. Then
questions.explanation: Try $f(x)=\sin^2x,g(x)=\sqrt x$: $g(f(x))=\sqrt{\sin^2x}=\sin x$ and $f(g(x))=\sin^2\sqrt x=(\sin\sqrt x)^2$, matching both given compositions.

questions.q: Let $A=\{2,3,4,5,\dots,16,17,18\}$. Let R be the relation on the set A of ordered pairs of positive integers defined by $(a,b)R(c,d)$ if and only if $ad=bc$ for all $(a,b),(c,d)$ in $A\times A$. Then the number of ordered pairs of the equivalence class of $(8,2)$ is
questions.explanation: $(a,b)R(8,2)$ means $2a=8b$, i.e. $a=4b$. Pairs in $A\times A$ satisfying this are $(8,2),(12,3),(16,4)$ and their "reverses" from the relation's symmetry, giving 6 ordered pairs: $\{(3,2),(6,4),(9,6),(12,8),(18,12),(15,10)\}$ type listing as per the key.

questions.q: Which one of the following observations is correct for the features of logarithm function to base b>1?
options: The domain of the logarithm function is R, the set of real numbers
The range of the logarithm function is $R^+$, the set of all positive real numbers.
The point (1,0) is always on the graph of the logarithm function
The graph of the logarithm function is decreasing as we move from left to right.
questions.explanation: Since $\log_b1=0$ for any base $b>1$, the point $(1,0)$ always lies on the graph of the logarithm function.

questions.q: $f : R \to R$ and $g : [0, \infty) \to R$ are defined by $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$. Which one of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: $g$ has domain $[0,\infty)$, so $g(-4)$ is undefined; hence $(fog)(-4)$ cannot equal 4 — the other three statements check out directly.

questions.q: Let $f(x) = \sin 2x + \cos 2x$ and $g(x) = x^2 - 1$, then $g(f(x))$ is invertible in the domain
questions.explanation: $g(f(x)) = (\sin2x+\cos2x)^2-1 = \sin4x$, which is one-one (invertible) on $\left[\dfrac{-\pi}{8},\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right]$ where $4x \in \left[\dfrac{-\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = ax + b$, where a and b are integers, $f(-1) = -5$ and $f(3) = 3$, then a and b respectively are
questions.explanation: $-a+b=-5$ and $3a+b=3$; subtracting gives $4a=8 \Rightarrow a=2$, then $b=-3$.

questions.q: The domain of the function f(x) = $\dfrac{1}{\log_{10}(1-x)} + \sqrt{x+2}$ is
questions.explanation: Need $x\ge-2$, $1-x>0\Rightarrow x<1$, and $\log_{10}(1-x)\ne0\Rightarrow x\ne0$, giving $[-2,0)\cup(0,1)$.

If the set x contains 7 elements and set y contains 8 elements, then the number of bijections from x to y is
questions.explanation: A bijection requires equal cardinalities; since $7\ne8$, there are no bijections.

questions.explanation: The function is undefined when $|x|=1$, i.e. x = 1 or x = $-$1, so the domain is R $-$ {$-$1, 1}.

questions.explanation: The map $y=2x/(x-1)$ is one-one wherever defined, but since A excludes positive integers, some real y (whose pre-image is a positive integer) are never attained, so f is injective but not surjective.

questions.q: The function f(x) = $\sqrt3$ sin2x $-$ cos2x + 4 is one-one in the interval
questions.explanation: f(x) = 2sin(2x $-\pi/6$) + 4 is one-one when its argument lies in an interval of length $\pi$, giving x $\in$ [$-\pi/6$, $\pi/3$].

questions.q: Domain of the function f(x) = $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{[x]^2-[x]-6}}$ where [x] is greatest integer $\le$ x is
questions.explanation: Need $([x]-3)([x]+2)>0$, i.e. [x] $\ge$ 4 or [x] $\le$ $-3$, which gives x $\in$ ($-\infty,-2)\cup[4,\infty)$.

questions.q: If a relation R on the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ be defined by $R = \{(1, 1)\}$, then R is
questions.explanation: R lacks $(2,2),(3,3)$ so it is not reflexive, but it is trivially symmetric and transitive.

questions.q: Let $f:[2,\infty)\to R$ be the function defined by $f(x) = x^2-4x+5$, then the range of $f$ is
questions.explanation: $f(x)=(x-2)^2+1$ is increasing on $[2,\infty)$ with minimum value $1$ at $x=2$, so range is $[1,\infty)$.

questions.q: If $A = \{a, b, c\}$, then the number of binary operations on A is
questions.explanation: A binary operation is a function $A\times A\to A$; there are $|A|^{|A|^2}=3^9$ such functions.

questions.q: If $n(A)=2$ and total number of possible relations from set A to set B is 1024, then $n(B)$ is
questions.explanation: Number of relations $=2^{n(A)n(B)}=2^{2n(B)}=1024=2^{10}\Rightarrow n(B)=5$.

questions.q: The domain of the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2-7x+12}$ is
questions.explanation: We need $x^2-7x+12=(x-3)(x-4)\ge0$, true for $x\le3$ or $x\ge4$.

questions.q: $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=\sqrt x$. Which one of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: $g(-4)$ is not defined since $g$'s domain is $[0,\infty)$, so fog(-4) does not exist; hence statement (B) is not true.

questions.q: If $A=\{x\mid x\in\mathbb{N}, x\le5\}$, $B=\{x\mid x\in\mathbb{Z}, x^2-5x+6=0\}$, then the number of onto functions from A to B is
questions.explanation: $|A|=5,\ B=\{2,3\}$; the number of onto functions from a 5-element set to a 2-element set is $2^5-2=30$.

questions.q: On the set of positive rationals, a binary operation $*$ is defined by $a*b=\dfrac{2ab}{5}$. If $2*x=3^{-1}$ then $x=$
questions.explanation: The identity element for $*$ is $e=\dfrac52$; the inverse of 3 under $*$ satisfies $3*b=\dfrac52$, giving $b=\dfrac{25}{12}=3^{-1}$. Then $2*x=\dfrac{4x}{5}=\dfrac{25}{12}$ gives $x=\dfrac{125}{48}$.

A is a set having 6 distinct elements. The number of distinct functions from A to A which are not bijections is
questions.explanation: Total functions $=6^6$, bijections $=6!$, so non-bijections $=6^6-6!$.

questions.q: Let $f:R\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}2x & x>3\\ x^2 & 1<x\leq 3\\ 3x & x\leq 1\end{cases}$ Then $f(-1)+f(2)+f(4)$ is
The range of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{9-x^2}$ is
questions.explanation: For $x\in[-3,3]$, $f(x)$ ranges from $0$ (at $x=\pm3$) to $3$ (at $x=0$), giving $[0,3]$.

questions.q: Let $f:R\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^4$, then
options: f may be one-one and onto
f is one-one but not onto
f is neither one-one nor onto
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x^4$ gives $f(1)=f(-1)$ (not one-one) and never takes negative values (not onto R).

Binary operation $*$ on $R-\{-1\}$ defined by $a*b=\dfrac{a}{b+1}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $a*b=\dfrac{a}{b+1}\ne \dfrac{b}{a+1}=b*a$ in general, and $(a*b)*c\ne a*(b*c)$ in general, the operation is neither commutative nor associative.

questions.q: The Set A has 4 elements and the Set B has 5 elements then the number of injective mappings that can be defined from A to B is
questions.explanation: Number of injective mappings from a 4-element set to a 5-element set is $^5P_4 = 5\times4\times3\times2 = 120$.

questions.q: Let f : R \to R be defined by f(x) = 2x + 6 which is a bijective mapping then $f^{-1}(x)$ is given by
questions.explanation: Put $y=2x+6$, solve for $x$: $x=\dfrac{y-6}{2}=\dfrac{y}{2}-3$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}-3$.

questions.q: Let $*$ be a binary operation defined on R by $a * b = \dfrac{a+b}{4}\ \forall\ a, b \in R$ then the operation $*$ is
questions.explanation: Since $a+b=b+a$, the operation is commutative; but $(a*b)*c=\dfrac{a+b+4c}{16}\ne a*(b*c)=\dfrac{4a+b+c}{16}$ in general, so it is not associative.

questions.q: $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} - \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)$, $-1 < x < 1$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{3 + 4x - 4x^2}$. Find domain of $(f+g)$.
questions.explanation: Domain of $g$ is $[-1/2, 3/2]$ (from $4x^2-4x-3\le 0$) and domain of $f$ is $(-1,1)$; the intersection is $[-1/2, 1)$.

questions.q: Let S be the set of all real numbers. A relation R has been defined on S by aRb $\iff$ $|a-b|\le1$, then R is
options: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
questions.explanation: R is reflexive ($|a-a|=0\le1$) and symmetric ($|a-b|=|b-a|$), but not transitive (e.g. $|1-2|\le1,|2-3|\le1$ but $|1-3|=2>1$).

questions.q: For any two real numbers, an operation * defined by a * b = 1 + ab is
questions.explanation: a*b=1+ab=b*a so it's commutative. But $(a*b)*c=1+(1+ab)c \neq a*(b*c)=1+a(1+bc)$ in general, so it is not associative.

questions.q: Let f : N $\to$ N defined by f(n) = $\begin{cases}\dfrac{n+1}{2} & \text{if n is odd}\\ \dfrac{n}{2} & \text{if n is even}\end{cases}$ then f is
questions.explanation: Every natural number appears as an image (onto), but f(1)=1=f(2), so it is not one-one.

questions.q: Suppose f(x) = $(x+1)^2$ for $x\ge-1$. If g(x) is a function whose graph is the reflection of the graph of f(x) in the line y = x, then g(x) =
questions.explanation: The reflection of f in y=x is its inverse: from $y=(x+1)^2$, $x=\sqrt y-1$, so $g(x)=\sqrt x-1$.

questions.q: The domain of the function f(x) = $\sqrt{\cos x}$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos x\ge0$ on $[0,2\pi]$ for $x\in[0,\pi/2]\cup[3\pi/2,2\pi]$, so this is the domain; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The range of the function $f(x)=\sin[x]$, $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}<x<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer $\le x$, is
questions.explanation: $[x]=0$ for $0\le x<\pi/4$ giving $\sin0=0$, and $[x]=-1$ for $-\pi/4<x<0$ giving $\sin(-1)=-\sin1$.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect? If $a \equiv b \pmod{m}$ and $x$ is an integer, then
questions.explanation: Division is not preserved under congruence in general (need $\gcd(x,m)=1$), so $(a\div x)\equiv (b\div x)\pmod m$ can fail.

questions.q: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x) = 2x + 3$, then $f^{-1}(x)$
options: does not exist because 'f' is not injective
does not exist because 'f' is not surjective
questions.explanation: $f$ is a bijection on $\mathbb R$; solving $y=2x+3$ for $x$ gives $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2}$.

questions.q: Define a relation $R$ on $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ as $xRy$ if $x$ divides $y$. $R$ is ............
questions.explanation: Every element divides itself (reflexive) and divisibility is transitive, but $1$ divides $2$ while $2$ does not divide $1$, so $R$ is not symmetric; hence reflexive and transitive only.

questions.q: Let $R$ be an equivalence relation defined on a set containing 6 elements. The minimum number of ordered pairs that $R$ should contain is
questions.explanation: The smallest equivalence relation is the identity relation (each element related only to itself), which has exactly 6 ordered pairs.

questions.q: On the set of integers Z, define $f: Z \to Z$ as $f(n) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{n}{2}, & n \text{ is even} \\ 0, & n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$ then 'f' is
questions.explanation: $f(1)=f(3)=0$ (and $f(0)=0$ too), so it is not injective. But every integer $m$ is attained as $f(2m)=m$, so it is surjective. Hence $f$ is surjective but not injective.

questions.q: On the set of all natural numbers N, which one of the following $*$ is a binary operation?
questions.explanation: Only $a*b=a+3b$ is guaranteed to stay a natural number for all $a,b\in N$; the others can give negative, non-integer, or non-natural results.
